ex: I tried to console her with a box of chocolates.

proportion

(noun). A part, share, or number considered in comparative relation to a whole.

ex: Children make up a large proportion of the world's population.

enjoyment

(noun). the state or process of taking pleasure in something

ex: It's sad if he never gets any enjoyment out of his job any more.

generally

(adverb). by or to most people

ex: He wants more money to be given to the arts generally.

household

(noun). A house and its occupants regarded as a unit.

ex: There are now on average 2.5 people per household in the state.

potentially

(adverb). With the capacity to develop

ex: Hepatitis is a potentially fatal disease.

research

(noun). the systematic investigation into and study of materials and sources

ex: His researches in the field of disease prevention produced unexpected results.

manufacturer

(noun). a person or company that makes goods for sale.

ex: They are the world's leading manufacturer of audio equipment.

design

(verb). decide upon the look and functioning of (a building, garment, or other object), by making a detailed drawing of it.

ex: Who designed this building/dress/furniture?

appropriate

(adjective). suitable for a certain purpose

ex: Is this film appropriate for small children?

consumer

(noun). A person who purchases goods and services for personal use.

ex: There was a rising worldwide consumption of consumer goods.

aid

(noun). Help, typically of a practical nature.

ex: He gets about with the aid of a walking stick.

specifically

(adverb). In a way that is exact and clear

ex: These jeans are designed specifically for women.

target

(noun). a result that you try to achieve

ex: I had four shots but I didn't even hit the target.

particular

(adjective). Used to single out an individual member of a specified group

ex: She wanted a particular type of cactus.

preschooler

(noun). a child who is not old enough to go to formal school

ex: If you keep a garden, make your preschooler the helper.

senior citizen

(noun). an elderly person, especially one who is retired and living on a pension

ex: I strongly object to being called a senior citizen

exploratory

(adjective). giving the reasons for something; intended to describe how something works or to make something easier to understand

ex: She's having some exploratory tests done to find out what's causing the illness.

formative

(adjective). having an important and lasting influence on the development of something or of somebody’s character

ex: She spent her formative years in Africa.

undertake

(verb). Commit oneself to and begin (an enterprise or responsibility);

ex: Students are required to undertake simple experiments.

audience

(noun). The assembled spectators or listeners at a public event

ex: She lectures to audiences all over the world.

electronic

(adjective). having or operating with components such as microchips

ex: The huge electronic scoreboard showed a replay of the last goal.

sufficiently

(adverb). enough for a particular purpose; as much as you need

ex: I was sufficiently close to hear what they were saying.

manipulate

(verb). Handle or control (a tool, mechanism, information, etc.) in a skilful manner.

ex: Throughout her career she has very successfully manipulated the media.

button

(noun). a small, usually circular object used to fasten something, for example a shirt or coat

ex: I did up/undid (= fastened/unfastened) the buttons on my blouse.

stumble

(verb). to hit your foot against something while you are walking or running and almost fall

ex: Running along the beach, she stumbled on a log and fell on the sand.

cognitive

(adjective). Relating to cognition.

ex: Some of her cognitive functions have been impaired.

stylus

(noun). a device on a record player that looks like a small needle and is placed on the record in order to play it

ex: Children use a pointed bone or metal stylus to make marks on the wax.

accurate

(adjective). correct in all details; exact.

ex: accurate information about the illness is essential

mimic

(verb). Imitate (someone or their actions or words),

ex: She was mimicking the various people in our office.

interaction

(noun). reciprocal action or influence.

ex: The play follows the interactions of three very different characters.

symbolically

(adverb). as a symbol; in a way that involves or uses symbols

ex: It is important symbolically for this museum to be in the right location.

object

(noun). A material thing that can be seen and touched.

ex: Several people reported seeing a strange object in the sky.

movement

(noun). An act of moving.

ex: He made a sudden movement and frightened the bird away.

connection

(noun). A relationship in which a person or thing is linked or associated with something else.

ex: The connection between smoking and heart disease is well known.

direct

(adjective). going straight to the point; frank

ex: Is there a direct train to Edinburgh?

vast

(adjective). extremely large

ex: A vast audience watched the broadcast.

majority

(noun). The greater number.

ex: The majority of the employees have university degrees.

profitable

(adjective). ​that makes or is likely to make money

ex: The company had to eliminate 200 jobs to stay profitable.

hardware

(noun). the machinery and electronic parts of a computer system

ex: Much of our existing military hardware is obsolescent.

rival

(noun). a person, company or thing that competes with another in sport, business, etc

ex: He beat his closest/nearest rival by 20 marks.

inappropriate

(adjective). not suitable or appropriate in a particular situation

ex: His casual behaviour was wholly inappropriate for such a formal occasion.

feature

(noun). a distinctive attribute or aspect of something.

ex: Our latest model of phone has several new features.

microphone

(noun). an instrument for converting sound waves into electrical energy variations which may then be amplified, transmitted, or recorded

ex: The interviewer asked her to speak into/use the microphone.

portability

(noun). the ability to be easily carried or move

ex: The advantage of the smaller model is its greater portability.

ripe

(adjective). fully grown and ready to be eaten

ex: Those bananas aren't ripe yet - they're still green.

platform

(noun). A raised level surface on which people or things can stand.

ex: The next train for Aberdeen will depart from platform 9.

investigate

(verb). Carry out research or study into a problem

ex: We are of course investigating how an error like this could have occurred.

specific

(adjective). clearly defined or identified

ex: The virus attacks specific cells in the brain.

characteristic

(noun). A feature or quality belonging typically to a person, place, or thing

ex: Unfortunately a big nose is a family characteristic.

market

(noun). an area or arena in which commercial dealings are conducte

ex: Are you sure there's a market for the product?

appeal

(verb). make a serious or urgent request, typically to the public

ex: The police are appealing to the public for any information about the missing girl.

crucial

(adjective). Decisive or critical, especially in the success or failure of something

ex: Her work has been crucial to the project's success.

assess

(verb). evaluate or estimate the nature, ability, or quality of.

ex: The insurers will need to assess the flood damage.

highlight

(noun). An outstanding part of an event or period of time.

ex: The report highlights the need for improved safety.

instruction

(noun). A direction or order.

ex: He gave me strict instructions to get there by eight o'clock.

express

(verb). to show or make known a feeling, an opinion,

ex: Her eyes expressed deep sadness.

consistently

(adverb). in a way that does not change.

ex: The president has consistently denied the rumours.

distract

(verb). Prevent (someone) from concentrating

ex: Don't distract her (from her studies).

cartridge

(noun). a tube or case containing explosive and a bullet or shot, for shooting from a gun

ex: He tried to eject the spent cartridge and reload.

capacity

(noun). The maximum amount that something can contain.

ex: The stadium has a seating capacity of 50,000.

representation

(noun). The action of speaking or acting on behalf of someone

ex: The farmers demanded greater representation in parliament.

title

(noun). The name of a book, composition, or other artistic work.

ex: There was a book I wanted to buy, but now I can't remember the title.

overview

(noun). a general review or summary of a subject.

ex: I'll give you a brief overview of what the job involves.

software

(noun). the programs and other operating information used by a compute

ex: He's written a piece of software that does your taxes for you.

behaviour

(noun). the way in which one acts or conducts oneself, especially toward others

ex: Her behaviour is often appalling.

impact

(noun). the action of one object coming forcibly into contact with another.

ex: The bullet explodes on impact (= when it hits another object).

method

(noun). A particular procedure for accomplishing or approaching something

ex: That method hasn't worked, so let's try your way.

criteria

(noun). A principle or standard by which something may be judged or decided.

ex: The Health Service should not be judged by financial criteria alone.

construct

(verb). Build or make (something, typically a building)

ex: The walls are constructed of concrete.

exclusively

(adverb). To the exclusion of others; only.

ex: This offer is available exclusively to our established customers.

reserve

(verb). keep sth for sb/sth

ex: These seats are reserved for the elderly and women with babies.

insatiable

(adjective). always wanting more of something; not able to be satisfied

ex: Nothing, it seemed, would satisfy his insatiable curiosity.

eagerness

(noun). Enthusiasm to do or to have something

ex: The book describes her eagerness for new experiences.

penetrate

(verb). to go into or through something

ex: Amazingly, the bullet did not penetrate his brain.

have a hunch

(phrase). to have an idea about what did, will, or should happen

ex: I had a hunch that you'd be here.

mechanics

(noun). the science of movement and force

ex: he looks at the mechanics of a car before the bodywork

mystery

(noun). Something that is difficult or impossible to understand or explain.

ex: The book tries to explain some of the mysteries of life.

query

(noun). a question, especially one asking for information or expressing a doubt about something

ex: What was their response to your query?

context

(noun). The circumstances that form the setting for an event, statement, or idea

ex: This small battle is very important in the context of Scottish history.

negotiate

(verb). Obtain or bring about by discussion.

ex: The government has refused to negotiate with the strikers.

minimal

(adjective). very small in size or amount; as small as possible

ex: There were no injuries and damage to the building was minimal.

perspective

(noun). A particular attitude towards something; a point of view

ex: Her attitude lends a fresh perspective to the subject.

verbal

(adjective). relating to words

ex: Do you have it down in writing, or was it just a verbal agreement?

cue

(noun). A thing said or done that serves as a signal to an actor or other performer

ex: They started washing up, so that was our cue to leave the party.

coordination

(noun). the act of making parts of something, groups of people, etc. work together in an efficient and organized way

ex: Gymnastics is a sport that requires a lot of coordination.
